make.label: A post or campaign
placeholders: What should we create, who is it for, and where will it be used?

publish.label: Post something I already have
placeholders: Which platforms, and when should it go out? Leave the caption empty and Claude writes one.
publish.filesHint: Give Claude the pictures or video in chat.

research.label: Research
placeholders: What should Claude find out, and what will you use it for?

analysis.label: Analyse a post or campaign
analysis.links: Links to the posts or campaign to analyse
placeholders: What do you want to learn from these posts?

breakdown.label: Break down a video
breakdown.links: The video to break down (a link, or a file on this computer)
placeholders: What do you want to learn from this video?
breakdown.filesHint: For a video file on your computer, give it to Claude in chat.

organic_post.name: Organic post
organic_post.purpose: One finished social post for Facebook, Instagram or TikTok: the picture or video, the caption and the posting details, ready for your approval.
examples: An Instagram post showing our new product
A TikTok video announcing the weekend offer
notFor: Paid ads, which need a budget and an ad plan (use Paid ad campaign)
A set of posts planned together (use Post series)

inputs.words: Who the post is for, when it differs from your brand's usual audience
An offer or message the post should carry
The web page people should go to
When it should go out
Things the post must say
Things the post must not say
A post or video you would like it to look like

organic_post.outputs: A delivery package for each post: the picture or video, the caption, hashtags and the posting details, ready to schedule or post.
organic_post.cost: Credits are spent only when pictures or video are made, and you approve the price first.

organic_series.name: Post series
organic_series.purpose: A set of related posts planned together, so they read as one campaign across platforms and days.
examples: Five Instagram posts for our product launch week
A month of Facebook posts about our team

inputs.words: Who the posts are for, when it differs from your brand's usual audience
An offer or message the posts should carry
The web page people should go to
When the posts should go out
Things the posts must say
Things the posts must not say
A post or video you would like them to look like

organic_series.outputs: A delivery package for each post in the series: the pictures or video, the captions, hashtags and the posting details.
organic_series.cost: Credits are spent only when pictures or video are made, and you approve the price first.

ugc_creative.name: Creator-style video
ugc_creative.purpose: A short video that looks like a customer or creator talking to the camera: ideas to pick from, a script, a storyboard and the finished video.
examples: A creator-style TikTok about why customers love our product
notFor: A video you already have (use Repurpose a video)

inputs.words: Who the video is for, when it differs from your brand's usual audience
An offer or message the video should carry
The web page people should go to
When it should go out
Things the video must say
Things the video must not say
A video you would like it to look like

ugc_creative.outputs: The finished video with its caption and the posting details, in a delivery package.
ugc_creative.cost: Credits are spent to make the video. You approve the price, then check a sample, before the rest is made.

paid_campaign.name: Paid ad campaign
paid_campaign.purpose: Ad creative and a campaign plan for paid social: audience, budget, placements and the setup steps. Nothing is switched on for you.
examples: A TikTok ad campaign for our spring sale
Instagram ads for a new product with a fixed budget
notFor: Ordinary posts that are not ads (use Organic post)
Changing a campaign that is already running

inputs.words: The most you want to spend
The web page people should go to
Who the ads are for, when it differs from your brand's usual audience
An offer or message the ads should carry
When the ads should start
An ad or video you would like them to look like

paid_campaign.outputs: The ad creative, the campaign plan and a checklist of setup steps for your ad manager.
paid_campaign.cost: Credits are spent only when pictures or video are made, and you approve the price first.

content_repurpose.name: Repurpose a video
content_repurpose.purpose: Turn a video you already have into new posts for other platforms, with new cuts and captions.
examples: Cut our launch video into three Reels
Make a TikTok from last month's webinar clip
notFor: A brand new video (use Creator-style video)
Posting a finished file as it is

inputs.words: The video to reuse, as a link or a file
Who the new posts are for, when it differs from your brand's usual audience
When the posts should go out
Things the posts must say
Things the posts must not say

content_repurpose.outputs: New cuts of your video with captions and the posting details, in a delivery package.
content_repurpose.cost: Credits are spent only when something new has to be made, and you approve the price first.

publish_post.name: Post something I already have
publish_post.purpose: Post a finished picture, a set of pictures or a video you already have, exactly as it is, with your own caption or one Claude writes. Nothing is researched or made, and no credits are spent.
examples: Post this video on our Instagram as a Reel tomorrow at 9 am
Put these three pictures on Facebook with my caption
notFor: Cutting, resizing or adding subtitles to a video (use Repurpose a video)
Making new pictures or video (use Organic post or Creator-style video)

inputs.words: Your own caption, posted word for word. Leave it out and Claude writes one
Whether the pictures or video were made with AI, so the post carries the platform's AI label
When it should go out

publish_post.outputs: Your pictures or video with the caption and the posting details, scheduled or saved as a draft in Metricool, or with a posting kit so you can post it yourself.
publish_post.cost: No credits. Nothing is made, so nothing is priced.

research.name: Research
research.purpose: A written report about a product, a brand or its competitors, with a source for every claim.
examples: What do customers say about our three closest competitors?
What is the market for a vitamin C serum in Singapore?
notFor: Looking at one post or one video you already have (use Post or campaign analysis or Video breakdown)

inputs.words: Links or files you want it to read

research.outputs: A report you can read on the board and download.

creative_analysis.name: Post or campaign analysis
creative_analysis.purpose: A written report on why a post or campaign works or does not, from the links or files you give.
examples: Why did our summer campaign get so many comments?
What is a competitor's best ad doing?
notFor: Taking apart one video scene by scene (use Video breakdown)
creative_analysis.outputs: A report you can read on the board and download.

video_breakdown.name: Video breakdown
video_breakdown.purpose: One video taken apart scene by scene: the shots, the spoken words, the on-screen text and how it is built from hook to call to action.
examples: Break down our best-performing launch video
How is this competitor's Reel put together?
notFor: Judging a whole campaign (use Post or campaign analysis)
video_breakdown.outputs: A report with a still for each scene, which you can read on the board and download.
